That conflated a source-local name-parts representation with a claim that this compiler equals an external canonical person. This vector asserts only the former. The unchanged primary citation and independently established Pat ordering provide a defensible finite contextual boundary; no new primary fact or person-identity link has been discovered.

source_specific_reasoning.finding: The primary citation explicitly reads 'Pat Livingston , Ed. and Douglas Smith, Compiler', followed on the next line by the NMFS/NOAA hierarchy. Both individual credits and their distinct editor/compiler qualifications are explicit, and the current reviewed legacy array already preserves Pat Livingston followed by Douglas Smith.

The exact NOAA forms 'Livingston, Pat' and 'Pat Livingston' independently establish natural given/family order for the first name in this very citation construction. Relevant AFSC institutional history provides database context, without expanding Pat or broadening the source's editor limitation.

The shared English citation coordinates two personal-name phrases with 'and', with each complete name followed by a comma and role. Neither name contains a surname-inversion comma. Reading Douglas as the given part and Smith as the family part follows the parallel natural-name construction anchored by Pat Livingston; the source supplies no competing boundary or inversion indicator for Douglas Smith. The role comma follows the whole name, so Compiler is not part of either name field. This is not an expressly labeled family/given field in the XML and is not represented as one.

The same original explicitly writes the separate contact as 'Bailey, Michael', showing a comma inside that inverted personal name. This punctuation contrast is limited contextual support for the citation reading, not permission to promote the contact or a universal name-order rule.

The modern fields retain exactly the already credited literal Pat Livingston and Douglas Smith in the same order. They add no middle initial, alias, expanded given name, ORCID, authority identifier, affiliation or relationship to another work. No equality with Douglas M. Smith, Doug Smith or D. M. Smith is asserted or needed.

contrary_readings_considered: Treating Douglas as the surname and Smith as the given name would require an unmarked reversal only for the second coordinated credit, despite the independently established first credit's order. No source feature or competing evidence supports that reading.

Treating the whole phrase Douglas Smith as an unresolved compound family name would likewise have no supporting source marker and would disregard the two-part personal-credit construction. This is not a claim that every two-token name can be split generally.

The source's absence of formal name-part labels limits the finding to a documented contextual inference; it does not itself establish a competing source ambiguity. The unresolved external-person identity question is retained but does not block these literal fields.
